definition: Maternal and child health: care for mothers before, during and after pregnancy, and for young children.
Primary health care: the first level of the health system: dispensaries, health centres and council hospitals.
SRA: a nationwide programme (from 2015) that scores Tanzanian facilities on the quality of their services.
Antenatal care: routine check-ups and services during pregnancy.
Basic Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care: core life-saving procedures for childbirth complications.
Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care: BEmONC plus surgery (caesarean) and blood transfusion.
Maternal and Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response: reviewing each death to prevent the next.
Integrated Management of Pregnancy and Childbirth: standard checklists, charts and protocols.
Integrated Management of Childhood Illness: guidelines for assessing and treating sick children.
A chart used during labour to track progress and spot danger signs early.
Kangaroo Mother Care: skin-to-skin care that keeps small or premature babies warm.
Postnatal care: care for mother and baby in the days and weeks after birth.
Health Facility Management Team: the group that runs and oversees a facility.
Quality Improvement Team: a facility team tasked with monitoring and improving care.
Adjusted odds ratio: how much more (or less) likely an outcome is, after accounting for other factors.
The lowest-level facility, offering outpatient services to about 10,000 people.
A mid-level facility serving a larger population, with some inpatient care.
